22521.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
22521.text: Momentum of a body is increased to three times its original value. By what percentage will its kinetic energy change?
22521.sol: The kinetic energy K of a body is related to its momentum p by the formula K = p^2 2m , where m is the mass of the body. Let the initial momentum be p₁ = p and the initial kinetic energy be K₁ = p^2 2m . The momentum is increased to three times its original value, so the new momentum is p₂ = 3p . The new kinetic energy K₂ is given by K₂ = p₂^2 2m = (3p)^2 2m = 9p^2 2m = 9K₁ . The change in kinetic energy is K = K₂ - K₁ = 9K₁ - K₁ = 8K₁ . The percentage change in kinetic energy is K K₁ 100 % = 8K₁ K₁ 100 % = 800 % .

79583.subject: Botany
options: The walls of diatoms are easily destructible
'Diatomaceous earth' is formed by the cell walls of diatoms
Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans
Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water
79583.sol: The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. A unique feature of diatom cells is that they are enclosed within a cell wall made of hydrated silicon dioxide called a frustule. These frustules show a wide diversity in form but are usually almost bilaterally symmetrical, hence the group name diatom. The symmetry is not perfect since one of the valves is slightly larger than the other, allowing one valve to fit inside the edge of the other.

Hence this is the right answer. While the lysosome is also involved in the transport of the hydrolytic enzymes, but it is not the major transport mechanism in the cell.

80585.subject: Botany
80585.text: What is the direction of micropyle in anatropous ovule?
80585.sol: Anatropous ovule is the most common type of ovule found in angiosperms. Here the ovule is inverted so that micropyle and hilum are present in the same line and the micropyle is directed downwards. Related Theory Micropyle is used for the various functions and processes of the egg or the seed plant. It is located at top of the seed or egg. It helps in absorbing the water at the time of germination of the seed. Through micropyle the root emerges out at the time of germination of the seed.

80668.subject: Botany
80668.text: Opening and closing of stomata is due to the:
options: change in Turgor pressure of guard cells.
80668.sol: The guard cells are filled with chloroplasts. The guard cells are rapidly influenced by changes in the turgor pressure that regulate the opening and closing of the stomata. In the case of dicot plants, the wall of the guard cells near the pore is thick and inelastic, whereas, the outer wall is thin, elastic and semi-permeable. When the turgor develops in the guard cells, the outer thin walls expand towards the outer side. This draws the thick inner walls slightly apart and creates a pore between the two guard cells
